articleTitle: A 5-Step Pedagogical Design for Engineering Courses
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 5-step pedagogical framework based on student-centered approach prepared for engineering educators’ mindset. This pedagogical framework has been applied and tested in various technical and engineering course units, been adapted for the new students of Generation Z. This framework can be a pedagogical toolbox in adapting the teaching and learning activities to the students’ needs, also measuring qualitatively the students’ dynamics and academic performance. So far, in the course units where this pedagogical method was applied there was a 20% increase of the success rate and a reduction of the drop-out rate between 5% to 15%.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effectiveness of Process Control Didactics Kits in Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: This paper deliberates some of the motivations for contemplating Kits in the theoretical-practical class of a Curricular Unit of Process Control to first year students of a Master Degree in Mechanical Engineering, alongside their purpose. Also, the perceptions of these students about the use of these kits in their learning process are discussed based on an online questionnaire developed for that purpose. According to students’ feedback, gathered by an anonymous online questionnaire, it was possible to investigate the effectiveness of the use of didactics kits in the learning of Process Control topics. The obtained results from the students perception are clearly positive and motivating to further uses of this type kit as portable laboratories.

articleTitle: Identifying career pathways to engineering education research in Australia
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: Currently there is limited understanding about the academic qualifications (or formal research training) which engineering education researchers possess, and which university departments they primarily reside in. The objective of this study is to capture information on these researcher characteristics via bibliographic analysis of publicly available sources.A list of 104 authors affiliated with Australian institutions who published in at least one of thirteen engineering education journals between 2018–2019 (inclusive) was retrieved. For each author, information about their qualifications and where they worked was compiled from available biographic information in their publications (e.g. often common in IEEE publications), ORCID profile, Scopus profile, the Australian TROVE database, and online university researcher profile. In total, 80 authors held a known PhD; 30 in technical engineering, 12 in engineering education, 3 in education, 21 in other disciplines, and 14 not specified. Of the 67 with known bachelor degrees, 69% were in engineering, the remainder widely varied. 92 authors worked in a university; 56 in engineering faculty, 9 in computing faculty, 13 in other faculty, 9 in teaching and learning departments, 4 in other capacities at a university. 4 authors did not work at a university.Our findings show that while a minority of engineering education researchers hold technical engineering PhD degrees, PhD theses on engineering education topics are becoming more widespread and we can predict a growing community of Australian engineering researchers. These data can assist with planning strategies for further increasing engagement with engineering education research in the Australian context.

articleTitle: Designing a Pedagogical Framework for Transnational Training
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: This paper presents the pedagogical framework designed to be implemented in an engineering transnational pilot training composed of eight training courses, taught in five different higher educational institutions across four European countries. The major unifying role played by the pedagogical framework between the various courses’ leaders, imposing the necessary discipline to integrate and align all the different training courses into the same transnational training project, is described.

articleTitle: Insights on time, gender and higher education pos-covid
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: The pandemic of covid-19 has created the backdrop for a significant change in academic time and, in particular, learning time. This short work in progress paper focuses on the results of a study involving a survey, open interviews with teachers and students and a meeting with students’ representatives at one university addressing student’s feelings concerning time management throughout Covid 19. The preliminary results suggest that students are more prone to accept the hybrid model, however pointing out some important questions, especially regarding gender issues. The paper concludes with some recommendations for the university to address students’ time management in gender equality plans, at different levels.

articleTitle: Current and future challenges for Engineering Education: voices from students, alumni, teachers and employers
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: Engineering education faces the pressure of providing updated scientific and technological training to students, as well as developing the necessary skills that allow them to respond to complex and interdisciplinary problems. The articulation of societal needs, the curriculum design, and the expectations of different stakeholders are setting a real challenge for Higher Education Institutions. To contribute to this discussion, this paper explores the perspectives of four different stakeholders – students, alumni, teachers, and employers – mapping their proximities and distances in talking a better training for engineering students using the example of mechanical and biomedical Engineering graduate and post-graduate courses. The overall vision of the four stakeholders interviewed allows the conclusion that there is a shared understanding of the challenges and some common pathways to accomplish them, although some disagreement about the strategies and the concrete action to be undertaken.

articleTitle: The need to include ethics education in engineering courses: looking to the role of engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: In contemporary times, the colossal role that engineering has had and still has in shaping social, economic and, especially, the use of natural resources has been recognized, hence in sustainability or unsustainability. The lack of anticipation of the potential negative consequences of the action of technology on society, has awakened to the need to incorporate ethical education in engineering courses, with the aim of promoting ethical responsibility for the technological creations created by engineering professionals and the consequences resulting from its application. Given this context, the study aimed to identify the main reasons that justify the need to include ethical education in engineering courses. For this, this objective was considered starting from the role that is attributed to engineering. Thus, the objective was to identify perspectives on the role of engineering and how these can support the inclusion of ethics education in engineering courses. The present study is a contribution to a better understanding and justification of the motivations for ethical education to be incorporated into engineering courses with a view to a responsible professional practice in the future. As such, it may be useful to all those who define the curriculum plans for engineering courses and for those who teach ethics in engineering courses.

articleTitle: Teaching Industrial Electronics: A Multidisciplinary Approach From the Analysis to a Laboratory Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for teaching industrial electronics engineering based on a multidisciplinary approach, encompassing all the required steps from the first context and analysis to a final experimental validation in laboratory. This project is developed within the scope of a curricular unit of the second year of the study plan for the degree in Industrial Electronics and Computer Engineering, at the University of Minho, Portugal. Specifically, the project consists in the development of a basic power electronics converter, namely the DC-DC boost-type, supported by a digital control based on the microcontroller 8051, based on the same work for all groups in terms of minimum requirements, specifications, and components. The paper presents the description and context of the curricular unit, the detailed description of the project, the methodology used for teaching the different subjects, the prototypes developed by the students, as well as the main exemplificative prototypes and obtained experimental results. All groups successfully developed the project (implemented the prototype and experimental results prove the operation of the converter) and were approved with an average pass rate of sixteen.

articleTitle: An overview of the experience in promoting professional environment internships in the Civil Engineering bachelor course of ISEP
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: In this article, the implementation of professional internships for students of the last curricular year of the Civil Engineering bachelor course of ISEP is presented. The project evolution over the last seven academic years is described in detail, including the procedures and requirements for students’ applications, the analysis of students’ performance, as well as the general acceptance of this consolidated strategy on Portuguese Civil Engineering bachelor courses from all parts involved. The management of this initiative in the last years of COVID-19 pandemics is also described. Some conclusions are drawn and future improvements are proposed, particularly possible modifications on the course curricular plan to allow extended contact periods of the students with the companies, as well as increasing the number of students following professional internships.

articleTitle: The Importance of Ethical Reasoning in Next Generation Tech Education
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is having a profound impact on human life, with both benefits and drawbacks in the societal, environmental, and technological realms. However, the ethical implications of AI are often not addressed in technology education, leaving future professionals with a lack of awareness in this area. This is concerning, as AI has the potential to greatly information delivery and affect human thinking, interaction, decision-making, and communication. To address these issues, there is a need for a framework to guide and help future AI developers make ethically responsible decisions. In this paper we propose a framework to foster ethical awareness and promote respect for human dignity and well-being, while also preventing harm. It is designed to be incorporated into technology education, ensuring that future professionals are equipped to navigate the ethical implications of AI. By prioritizing ethical reasoning in technology education, we can build a better and more responsible AI industry, ensuring that AI can provide benefits for society and does not cause harm. Additionally, a tech industry that values ethics and social responsibility will be better equipped to build technology that serves the public interest, rather than solely maximizing profits. Teaching ethical reasoning in technology education is a crucial step in preparing future professionals to make informed and ethical decisions in the development and use of AI systems. It will lead to a better and more responsible AI industry that benefits all of society.

articleTitle: Active learning methods in the discipline of Introduction to Control and Automation Engineering: Meaningful Learning and higher engagement in the Engineering course
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: The lack of student engagement with their chosen undergrad course is something that deserves attention, whether to motivate the student regarding their chosen course or to prevent them from dropping out. In the field of engineering, the impact of attrition is concerning due to its high technological investments. The Control and Automation Engineering course fits into this scenario, especially when offered at a public institution. Active learning methodologies were employed in the pedagogical planning of this study, promoting meaningful learning through the completion of an engineering project with incoming students and allowing them to experience the peculiarities and demands that are natural to the field of engineering. The engagement of incoming students with the course can be evidenced through the satisfaction rate of over 90% of the respondents towards the proposed active learning methodologies. The attrition rates obtained in the researched classes compared to those of the national average signals towards the potential of active learning methodologies for increasing students’ commitment within the course, although further studies are necessary to confirm this improvement.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Students’ academic performance in a master engineering course
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: The main objective of this work is to understand what variables may have impact in the academic performance of the students. Descriptive statistics and Kruskal-Wallis H test, a rank-based non-parametric test were used to verify if there were statistically significant differences between two or more groups of an independent variable on a dependent variable such as the final grade average the number of ECTS credits obtained or the dropout rate. The nationality as well as the bachelor origin has impact on the average grade. Also, the age of the enrolled students and the type of bachelor’s degree (engineering vs. non engineering) has impact on the dropout rate of the master course. A longitudinal analysis was also performed as a useful approach for helping to better understand students’ performance. Tracking students as a group over a specified period allowed the master course coordination to have a better perception and identify students who are succeeding or falling behind.

articleTitle: Enhancing engineering education by means of the promotion of entrepreneurial mindsets and attitudes for societal challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: The development of skills and awareness of entrepreneurship and innovation topics in engineering curricula has been growing by diverse measures, such as by means of team-working sessions towards real-world problems, promotion of problem-solving assignments, and external initiatives to exploit ideas and to promote the development of new products or services. This paper addresses an approach taken as a complementary, extracurricular, education program together with a Product Development Project course, activities promoted by a joint initiative of several European universities in the form of the “Start for Future” (SFF) program. This initiative allowed students to explore the innovation and entrepreneurship dimensions of their ongoing projects with tandem teams from other institutions and external experts. The potential impact of this integrated, international, program is reviewed, considering both the work developed by students as well as analyzing the competences acquired during the extra-curricular activities. These initiatives proved to attain a positive effect on students and the learning process, stimulating entrepreneurial mindsets and attitudes, as well as complementing the training of the student on a number of transferable competences that are crucial for future engineers.

articleTitle: Do transferable skills matter for engineering students?
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: Transferable skills are becoming increasingly important, due to a progressively more competitive labor market in an ever-changing world. Particularly in the engineering sphere, it is even more obvious, as technical skills need transferable skills to have value. Increasing importance is being given by organizations and employers to transferable skills of their employees. Consequently, this study has two main goals: (1) analyze and determine how important engineering students consider transferable skills for their future career and (2) translate, adapt, and validate the Generic Skills Perception Questionnaire (GSPQ) - level of importance - for the Portuguese context. The scale was voluntarily answered by a sample of 219 engineering students from a Portuguese University. Descriptive measures were used to verify the perceived importance of the transferable skills of engineering students for their professional future. The scale GSPQ was validated for the Portuguese context through confirmatory factor analysis. Practical implications were drawn, namely the need to (re)structure the curricular units that are vital to a successful engineer development.

articleTitle: Testing OpenFOAM Computational Fluid Dynamics simulation of heat transfer and fluid flow in a mechanical engineering bachelor degree
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: Nowadays, countless areas in the domain of mechanical engineering practice can benefit from the use of Computational Fluid Dynamics techniques. Currently, at the Energy branch of the master’s degree in mechanical engineering at Instituto Superior de Engenharia do Porto, Computational Fluid Dynamics is only formally addressed in the first semester of the final year. In many cases, this prevents the students from promptly acquiring the necessary knowledge to embrace a master’s thesis or research project in this field. A possible way to minimise this problem was tested by exposing the students to the Computational Fluid Dynamics world earlier. Thus, in the curricular year 2022/2023, two optional simulation cases with a 35% weight in the final grade of a Heat Transfer course were proposed to the third-year students of the bachelor’s degree.For this purpose, an educational intervention following an action research methodology was implemented. A questionnaire was used to collect students’ feedback. Qualitative grades of the project reports and the discussion sessions corroborated students learning. Considering the students’ grades and that their feedback was in accordance with the complexity of the two simulation cases, we conclude that this education intervention was successful and that Computational Fluid Dynamics can be introduced earlier.

articleTitle: Blending Hands-on Learning and Team-based Learning in Soil Mechanics: Phase Relationships for Soils
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: This paper reports the application of hands-on learning and team-based learning to increase learning and promote deep understanding of key topics in Soil Mechanics. The pedagogical practice was implemented during first semester of 2022/2023 on an introductory course on Soil Mechanics at the Civil Engineering degree at the University of Aveiro, Portugal. The key topics covered were phase relations for soils. Combining the advantages of hands-on activities and team-based learning may help engineering students to close the gap between theory, previous knowledge and real-life situations, while promoting a structured form of learning deeper and developing critical thinking. The four sequenced activities of team-based learning included were: 1) preparation; 2) readiness assurance testing; 3) feedback; 4) application of knowledge through problem solving activities. The resources prepared for the hands-on and for the team-based learning activities are presented, together with the strategies used to assess the success of blending hands-on and team-based learning. The results obtained by students on an individual quiz and later on the same quiz tackled in groups are presented and discussed. The group discussion led to higher percentage of correct answers in the quiz. At the end of the session most students achieved the predefined learning outcomes. Based on the students’ perceptions collected, the receptivity of the students to the model is very good.

articleTitle: Reforming Doctoral Education through Immersive Ph.D. Training Weeks
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: Ph.D. training worldwide, including Doctoral education in Engineering fields, has been in trouble for some time [1]. These last turbulent times (Pandemic, energy, inflation, and war crises) have only increased the problems previously reported by the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> cycle students and early career researchers, including chronic lack of support and poor-quality supervision, with senior researchers rarely trained in mentorship [2]. It is also reported that Ph.D. candidates are inadequately prepared for the cross-disciplinary working and large teams that characterize cutting-edge science today. In the last two decades, opposite decisions took place in Europe concerning the curricula of Doctoral programs. In the years 2010s, a large number of classes was added to the Ph.D.s, contributing to almost residual time for thesis research in the first year of the programmes. However, ten years later, an abrupt change took place and almost all classes were removed from the Ph.D. curricula, creating a void in (hard and soft skills) training and leaving all the responsibility of training to the supervisor. Ph.D. students reported guidance and isolation issues in the first year. Moreover, today’s little Ph.D. training is fully dedicated to the obtention of their Ph.D. and not to their role in society after the Ph.D. defense [3].This work discusses a new approach to doctoral STEAM education in the actual doctoral programs’ framework, where few classes take place. This approach considers a novel Ph.D. training, both hard and soft skills development, through special intensive weeks, called Immersive Weeks. In these, distributed during the first year, Ph.D. students exclusively participate in several workshops, acquiring the tools for accomplishing both a successful Ph.D. and a future job. Pilots of this approach took place at the University of Aveiro with large success, while some improvement suggestions have also been pointed out by students.

articleTitle: Network of Good Practices to Reduce Gender Gap in Engineering Courses
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: The main objective of this study is to develop a tool to diagnose how to improve the network of good practices to reduce gender gap in engineering education that was created by the working group in gender and diversity of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education. The paper makes an introduction of the topic and the reasons for the creation of the network of good practices. The descriptive analysis of the network was performed as well as the developed work made by the members within the two years since its creation. To enlarge, improve and strengthen the network a qualitative survey was developed to capture the perceptions and practices of the members and better understand what to do to improve the effectiveness of the network. Barriers and enablers of an informal good practices network for collaborative and cooperative work in online settings were identified and used to develop the survey. The study focused three main areas related to the domain of the network, the members, and the practices. The study is meaningful, and it contributes to open avenues to develop future actions with the goal of improving the effectiveness of the network.

articleTitle: Design of a STEAM professional master’s programme supported by project-based learning methodologies
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: The project-based learning (PBL) pedagogical approach is a powerful tool for promoting deep knowledge and skill development in students through meaningful, real-world activities. This paper presents a professional master’s cycle of studies designed for science, technology, engineering, arts/humanities and mathematics (STEAM) teachers, supported by PBL methodologies. With this cycle of studies, we intend to promote the development of digital skills, enabling teachers and instructors to apply such technology in innovative teaching strategies. After the various stages of development, we achieved a certification for the cycle of studies. Based on the data obtained, we were able to create a cycle of studies approved by the competent institutions. Also, we can state that the cycle of studies designed can respond to the teachers’ digital training needs. Furthermore, we designed the cycle of studies with the PBL approach, as an innovative pedagogical approach that can promote the development of important job skills for teachers in order to increase the learner’s motivation.

articleTitle: Stimulating the learning of Ethics and Critical Thinking: a class given by students, for students
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: This paper presents the results of the work developed by two teams that were challenged to give a lecture to theirs peers about critical thinking and ethics in the context of an elective course. This elective course is running for the second year and it is offered to all students in a Portuguese university. The main idea of this course is to stimulate students to learn about contents normally not approached in their compulsory courses. This course is called “Preparing Generation Z: beyond technologies (Z-Tec)”. Themes discussed in the classes are related with personal skills such as critical thinking, communication, leadership, teamwork as well as ethics or even more practical themes like CV design or job interviews behavior. Such competencies could be the key factor for differentiation in a technological career. In Z-Tec classes active learning methodologies (e.g. practical exercises, debates, seminars and reflective activities) and teamwork are used. Each team must develop/discuss a topic chosen by them and lecture it on the class. From the six teams, two discussed critical thinking and ethics and the creative way they approached these both themes is presented in this paper. Presenting this, the authors want to show that with the right stimulus, students are capable to teach and learn with their peers.

articleTitle: Near-peer mentoring program implementation in STEM higher education
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: To increase academic success in an engineering higher education institution a near-peer mentoring program was designed for first year students and implemented. First-year students face several challenges due to a transition to a different academic approach, sometimes the need to adopt new study methods, or live in a new city. For many students the increase of responsibility and autonomy happens simultaneously with the enrolment at the higher education institution, and with the beginning of adult life. It’s common to a first-year student to feel an overwhelmed sensation that can be converted in enthusiasm or run-down. The mentoring programs can help to cope with these students, contribute to their academic success and mitigate early dropouts. In this paper the design process and the development stages during the implementation of a near-peer mentoring program are described.

articleTitle: Common skills in projects from different areas of knowledge: developing the professional profile
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference of the Portuguese Society for Engineering Education (CISPEE)
abstract: The undergraduate programs in Brazil follow national guidelines in which are stated the competences that need to be developed along the course by students. Schools may include other specific competencies in order to meet their own demands. To achieve an integrative approach between the Engineering, Design and Administration programs, interacting in multidisciplinary projects, one institution proposed a list of convergent competencies based on the tripod of innovation aimed at empowering its students for a global scenario. In this work is presented the process of building this list of competencies for the training of professionals in these three areas, with an updated and innovative profile. The research method was at first step, the documental analysis, that allowed to identify a convergent list of competences. From this list it was possible to build the questionnaire to survey the competences that was indicated by instructor in their projects and, that will be used too to gather perceived by students after to fulfill the projects, and to evaluate how close are the perception of students with stated by instructors.
